description: The legislative register at nbs.sk/dohlad-nad-financnym-trhom/legislativa/narodna-legislativa/ exposes a filter UI (name/number, year, area, document type) but the underlying result list did not render in the fetched content — it is likely populated by JavaScript or a POST/query endpoint.

This cell covers NBS only. Adjacent SK regulatory actors that co-produce banking/payments rules and deadlines were not scouted: Ministerstvo financií SR (author of the underlying zákony), NR SR (parliamentary legislative process for e.g. zákon o platobných službách 492/2009, zákon o bankách 483/2001), Rezolučná rada, and the Slovak Banking Association (SBA).

A large share of SK banking supervision originates at ECB/SSM, EBA and the EU level, and NBS acts partly as transposer/adopter. The ECB/SSM and EBA source layer was out of this cell's scope and was not scouted.

Deadlines are embedded in prose and PDFs across at least five distinct NBS streams (opatrenia účinnosť dates, consultation comment windows, EBA guideline application dates, DORA register submission windows, reporting calendars). No single structured deadline source exists.

NBS serves many documents via opaque UUID paths (nbs.sk/dokument/<uuid>/stiahnut) and retains a partially migrated legacy tree (www.nbs.sk/_img/documents/...). Both are fragile anchors for long-term monitoring.
Several candidates (slov-lex LP pages, lrv.rokovania.sk, fininfo.sk, mfsr.sk subtrees) were identified from search results and not confirmed by successful direct fetch in this pass.
EU-level consultation feeds that drive SK transposition deadlines (EBA, ECB/SSM, EU Commission 'Have your say', EPC for payments) were out of this cell's national scope and were not scouted here.
No structured extraction path was established for 'vyhodnotenie pripomienok' (comment-evaluation tables) which state which objections were accepted and whether the effective date moved.
Non-bank payments actors that also file comments (fintech/e-money associations, SK Fintech association, consumer bodies) were not mapped; only the bank association (SBA) was captured.
LexAPI and LexEPI commercial terms, pricing and redistribution rights were not established.

Group-parent newsrooms (Erste Group for Slovenska sporitelna, Intesa Sanpaolo for VUB, Raiffeisen Bank International for Tatra banka, KBC for CSOB) were not systematically searched; group-level vendor deals often cover the SK subsidiary without a SK-language announcement.

Vendor-side press-release archives and newswires (vendor /news, /press, /newsroom subtrees; SK PR wires such as TASR/SITA business services) were only sampled, not enumerated. These typically carry the win announcement months before a polished case study exists.

Professional-network and job-market signals (vendor and bank hiring for named platforms, consultancy staffing for regulatory-reporting programmes) were not covered; these often reveal a platform choice before any announcement.

Big-4 and consultancy SK practice pages (KPMG SK, Deloitte CZ/SK, PwC, EY) publish DORA/NIS2/regulatory-readiness material for the SK market and are themselves compliance-service vendors to banks, but were not profiled as sources in this slice.

All candidate URLs in this slice were identified via search-result metadata and summaries; none were independently fetched and confirmed by this agent, and several (Tempest http-only, FinStat paid tiers) may have access constraints.

Procurement profiles for second-tier state-linked financial actors (SZRB, Eximbanka's ÚVO profile ID, Fond ochrany vkladov, Garančný fond investícií, Sociálna poisťovňa's II-pillar systems, DataCentrum) were not individually resolved to ÚVO profile IDs.
No CPV code set has been fixed for this cell, so tender filtering is currently keyword-based and will be noisy.
Local-language coverage was achieved for procurement portals and actors, but no Slovak glossary was built for the regulatory subject-matter terms that would appear inside tender descriptions.
No historical backfill strategy is defined; only forward-looking monitoring is described.

Documentation attached to tenders (súťažné podklady, opis predmetu zákazky, vysvetlenia) — where the regulatory justification actually lives — often sits behind platform registration on JOSEPHINE and EPVO.

Large SK/CEE firms with known Bratislava banking practices — Dentons, Wolf Theiss, Allen & Overy/A&O Shearman, Squire Patton Boggs, Eversheds Sutherland, bnt, Ružička and Soukeník-Štrpka — were confirmed as active in SK banking/finance but their individual insight/alert feeds were not located and profiled in this pass.

Payments-specific adviser commentary (PSD2/PSD3/PSR, instant payments regulation, payment institution and e-money licensing, interchange) is thin relative to AML and DORA coverage; only one SK practice page was found squarely on payments/e-money.
Non-Big-Four compliance consultancies operating in SK (e.g. Grant Thornton, BDO, Mazars/Forvis, RSM, plus local AML/regtech advisories) were not searched in this pass.

No RSS/Atom feed was confirmed for any candidate; all suggested methods assume HTML crawling. LinkedIn is likely the fastest-publishing channel for SK adviser alerts (KPMG SK LinkedIn surfaced in search) but was not assessed for access/legality.

No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-tested; several entries (ULC Legal bulletin archive, LEXANTE blog, bpv article listing, Taylor Wessing and Clifford Chance index pages) are inferred hub URLs rather than observed article URLs.
Media coverage of supervisory enforcement (sanctions, licence withdrawals, AML fines) against SK institutions is not established by this pass.
Several highest-value outlets (Denník N, Index SME, HN, TREND) are paywalled, so full-text longitudinal monitoring is not possible from open crawling alone.
No commercial media-monitoring/clipping aggregator for Slovakia was verified in this pass, despite such services being the standard route to archived items that later vanish.
Non-web media channels — podcasts, newsletters by Slovak banking journalists, LinkedIn/X commentary by NBS and SBA figures — were not covered.

Career pages of several major SK banks and of non-bank PSPs/e-money institutions were not individually located in this pass — VÚB, ČSOB SK, 365.bank, Prima banka, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK branch, mBank SK, plus payment institutions (e.g. acquirers, PISP/AISP licence holders on the NBS register).
Job ads and event agendas are ephemeral — postings disappear on close and agenda pages are overwritten for the next edition, so no historical baseline exists.

Slovak job ads at international banking shared-service centres in Bratislava are often written in English, while regulator and training material is Slovak-only; a single-language crawl will systematically miss one half.

Public-sector and parliamentary speech channels adjacent to NBS were not covered — Ministry of Finance SR officials' conference remarks, and NBS supervisors speaking at third-party events where only the organiser publishes the agenda.
Several candidate URLs (finweek.sk/program, trend.sk award landing, profesia keyword URLs) were derived from search results rather than fetched in this pass, and one is paywalled.

Resolution-authority reporting (Rada pre riešenie krízových situácií / NBS resolution function: SRB liability data templates, MREL reporting, ex-ante contribution data submissions) was not covered in this pass.
AML/CFT reporting to Finančná spravodajská jednotka (FSJ, NAKA) and PSD2 fraud reporting operational detail were not enumerated, though fraud data is referenced in the PI licensing condition.
AnaCredit (Register bankových úverov a záruk) and the forthcoming Integrated Reporting Framework (IReF) national implementation timeline for SK were not researched.

Slov-Lex (the official SK legal information system with machine-readable ELI/API access) was not directly profiled as the canonical carrier of Act 483/2001 (banks), Act 492/2009 (payment services) and Act 540/2001 (state statistics) reporting mandates.
Regulatory-reporting vendors serving Slovak banks/PSPs (which reveal obligation changes early through release notes and webinars) were not scouted.

No SK constitutional/judicial layer was covered: Ústavný súd SR (constitutional challenges that can suspend or annul a financial-sector provision, e.g. bank levy litigation) and NS/NSS SR case-law databases.

English-language coverage of the SK legislative machinery is thin by nature: Slov-Lex, NR SR, LRV and rokovania.gov.sk publish essentially only in Slovak. The only substantive EN entry points found were the NBS English legislation pages and N-Lex.

Industry-side actors that appear inside the MPK comment files were not separately scouted: Slovenská banková asociácia (SBA), Asociácia poskytovateľov platobných služieb / fintech bodies, and Republiková únia zamestnávateľov, all of which publish their own positions on banking and payments drafts.
No confirmed identifier that joins a Slov-Lex LP/PI process to an NR SR parliamentary print (CPT/MasterID) to the final Z. z. number. Each system uses its own key.
Regional/EU upstream layer was out of scope for this cell but is the origin of most SK banking rules: EUR-Lex transposition deadlines and EBA/ECB acts drive the tabuľka zhody attached to SK drafts.
Terms of service / robots.txt for slov-lex.sk, nrsr.sk, rokovania.sk and the commercial mirrors were not examined in this pass.
AMLA (the new EU AML Authority, Frankfurt) was not reached as a source in this pass; its selection of directly supervised entities and its SK-facing guidance are not yet covered.

EU-level consultation calendars (Commission 'Have your say', EBA public consultations, ESAs joint consultations) were not individually catalogued, so forward-looking deadline signals are under-covered.

The SK pre-legislative comment procedure (medzirezortné pripomienkové konanie) on Slov-Lex was identified but not exercised — no confirmed query pattern for locating MF SR financial-market transposition bills.
CRR3/CRD6 (banking package) SK application and the EU MiCA/crypto and Basel output-floor deadlines were not searched in this cell.
Two key registers (EBA EUCLID payment institutions register, Slov-Lex search) are client-side applications whose collectability was not established.

Law-enforcement and prosecution side of financial crime (NAKA/Úrad kriminálnej polície, Generálna prokuratúra SR, Kriminálny úrad finančnej správy) was not covered with a verified source in this pass.

The concrete reporting mechanics for obliged entities — NOO (neobvyklá obchodná operácia) report forms, the FSJ electronic reporting channel, and statutory reporting deadlines — were not pinned to a specific verified URL.
VASP/crypto AML registration and supervision in SK (a fast-moving segment adjacent to payment firms, now under MiCA + AML Regulation) is only indirectly represented.
MONEYVAL, FATF and AMLA sources in this cell are English-only; no Slovak-language official translation channel for these evaluations was identified.
No SK-specific AML consultation calendar was found; consultations surface ad hoc via Slov-Lex LP/PI records and professional-chamber alerts.

Full texts of NBS consumer-protection decisions live on legacy /_img/documents/_dohlad/ofsrozhodnutia/ PDF paths whose relationship to the current 'Výroky právoplatných rozhodnutí' filter UI was not established in this pass.

No SK-specific court-decision channel was profiled for conduct/data-protection litigation against banks (e.g. the Ministry of Justice decisions portal, Najvyšší správny súd SR review of NBS/ÚOOÚ decisions).
English coverage of this cell is thin: only the NBS /en/ mirror was located, and no English pages were confirmed for ÚOOÚ, SOI decisions or the ARS bodies.

Slov-Lex (Zbierka zákonov + legislative process portal) was referenced indirectly but not profiled as a candidate in this slice, and the EDPB register of Art.60/Art.65 outcomes involving the Slovak authority was not searched.
Slovak Banking Association (SBA) conduct codes, complaint statistics from individual banks' ombudsman/complaint reports, and insurer/lender association conduct codes were not explored.

SK card processing and ATM/POS infrastructure operators (e.g. the ancillary systems settling in TARGET-SK such as the card clearing operator, and CDCP SR) were only surfaced indirectly via NBS text; no dedicated operator sources were profiled.
No NBS-run public consultation channel for payments (as distinct from MF SR legislative consultation) was located.
E-money/PI prudential reporting and statistical outputs (NBS payment statistics under ECB Regulation 2020/2011) were not covered in this pass.
Scheme-rulebook layer (EPC, Visa, Mastercard) is English-only; there is no Slovak-language early-warning channel for scheme deadlines other than SBA and press coverage after the fact.
No historical/archival snapshot source for SK registers was identified — registers show current state only, so entrants and revocations are invisible retrospectively.

Enforcement/sanction decisions (rozhodnutia NBS, sankcie, odňatie povolenia) as a structured list were not located in this pass, though the crypto licensing page shows NBS publishes decision-stage information.
Several EU-level registers (EBA, ECB) exist only in English, and their SK entity names may not match the Slovak legal names used in ORSR/NBS.
Access terms / robots policies for regfap.nbs.sk, regver.nbs.sk and subjekty.nbs.sk were not checked, so scraping legality and rate limits are unconfirmed.

No association-level archive of past position papers was identified; SBA and the fintech association publish rolling news without an obvious document repository, and site search/pagination depth is unknown.

The payments-specific and capital-markets-specific association layer is thin: no SK payments-institution association found, AOCP unaddressable, and the crypto bodies (SKMA, Blockchain Slovakia) unverified.
Member lists for SBA, SFA and ALS were located as URLs but their actual contents were not extracted in this pass, so the pointer value is identified but not yet realised.
English-language mirrors exist for SBA (/en/) and AFISP (/en/) but were not compared against the Slovak originals; other associations appear Slovak-only.
A meaningful share of association output flows through LinkedIn and Facebook, both of which are login-walled and ToS-restricted for automated collection.

Pre-legislative influence (PI — predbežná informácia stage, ministry working groups, NBS advisory bodies) is only partially covered; associations are known to comment at the PI stage but no systematic feed for this was identified.

Smaller/foreign-branch banks operating in SK (mBank SK branch, Fio banka pobočka, J&T banka pobočka, Privatbanka, Oberbank, Komerční banka pobočka, Wüstenrot/ČSOB stavebná sporiteľňa, Prvá stavebná sporiteľňa) were not individually scouted for disclosure and T&C-change surfaces.
Remuneration disclosures (zverejňovanie o odmeňovaní), ESG/Pillar 3 ESG templates, MREL and recovery-plan summaries, and country-by-country reporting were not separately located for each bank.
Superseded T&C versions are only partially retrievable — Tatra banka keeps an explicit /files/archiv/ tree, but SLSP, VÚB, ČSOB and 365.bank appear to overwrite or rotate current versions.
English-language versions of SK bank T&C-change notices were barely present; almost all change notices and Pillar 3 texts are Slovak-only (VÚB publishes some _SJ/_SK variants only).
None of the listed URLs were confirmed live in this pass; several (SLSP zverejnenia folder, Tatra banka documents hub, legacy NBS measure path) were inferred from child assets or search snippets.
